findings.current: These bastards were trying to steal monsters I had already taken down.
findings.defect: The draft says the monsters had already been taken down, but all four ogres are still alive. 다 잡은 means Taekyung already had them effectively beaten or claimed, not that he had killed them.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves Taekyung’s claim that the ogres were effectively his kills without contradicting their continued presence in the scene.
findings.replacement: These bastards were trying to steal mobs I already had dead to rights.
findings.source: 이 새끼들이 어디서 다 잡은 몹을 스틸하려고.

findings.current: “I asked him, and he said we could talk after he finished butchering.”
findings.defect: The explicit subject 정 팀장 shows that someone else—Captain Yoo—is reporting what Team Leader Jeong asked. Changing it to “I asked him” assigns the line to Jeong and alters the speaker.
findings.rationale: This retains the stated subject and correctly distinguishes Captain Yoo’s contribution from Team Leader Jeong’s preceding answer.
findings.replacement: “Team Leader Jeong asked him, but he said they could talk once he finished butchering.”
findings.source: “정 팀장이 물어봤는데, 우선 도축 끝내고 얘기하자더군요.”

findings.current: Both wore Special Forces uniforms beneath armor. They were, well, the stereotypical outfits of soldiers and Hunters.
findings.defect: The source presents the two men in their respective characteristic outfits—one in a Special Forces uniform and the other in armor. The draft instead puts both men in uniforms beneath armor and then ungrammatically calls the men “outfits.”
findings.rationale: The respective clothing establishes their visibly different roles while preserving the narrator’s hesitant 뭐랄까 beat.
findings.replacement: One wore a Special Forces uniform and the other armor. They were, well, dressed like a stereotypical soldier and Hunter.
findings.source: 각기 특전사 군복에 갑옷을 입은 그들은 뭐랄까, 전형적인 군인과 헌터의 복장이었다.

findings.defect: The comparison is reversed. The reporter confirms that Taekyung said C-rank rather than C-cup; the draft instead asks whether he means C-cup rather than C-rank.
findings.rationale: This restores the direction of the clarification and supports Taekyung’s ensuing reaction to the reporter looking at his chest.

findings.current: They were falling from a height of more than twenty meters. At that distance, even Hunters equipped with magic gear would put considerable strain on their knees when they landed.
findings.defect: “At that distance” changes a vertical height into generic distance, and “magic gear” departs from the established Equipment terminology.
findings.rationale: The source specifically attributes the landing strain to the height and uses the established term 장비.
findings.replacement: They were falling from a height of more than twenty meters. At that height, even Hunters outfitted with magical Equipment were bound to strain their knees on landing.
findings.source: 20m가 넘는 높이. 이 정도면 아무리 마법 장비를 갖춘 헌터라고 해도 무릎에 무리가 가기 마련이다.

findings.current: “You’re only a team member when it suits you, huh? A military reporter? Usually you’re always hungover. Did you get this excited just because you landed one scoop?”
findings.defect: The fragment “A military reporter?” loses the contrast in Jeong’s jab: Kim claims team membership only at useful moments while otherwise acting as a correspondent. This weakens their antagonistic familiarity and makes the dialogue incoherent.
findings.rationale: The replacement restores the contrast between opportunistic team membership and Kim’s usual reporter role while retaining Jeong’s pointed but familiar register.
findings.replacement: “You’re only part of the team at times like this, huh? The rest of the time, you’re a military correspondent. You’re usually drowning in a hangover—aren’t you getting a little too excited just because you landed one scoop?”
findings.source: “이럴 때만 팀원이고 군종 기잡니까? 평소에는 맨날 숙취에 찌들어 계시더니 특종 하나 잡았다고 너무 좋아하시는 거 아니에요?”

findings.current: Three question marks seemed to appear on their faces at the same time. I couldn’t help letting out a hollow laugh.
findings.defect: 실소 is an involuntary chuckle rather than a hollow laugh, and the explicit amused thought 이거 재밌네 is omitted.
findings.rationale: This restores both Taekyung’s spontaneous amusement and the short internal punchline.
findings.replacement: Three question marks seemed to appear on their faces at the same time. I couldn’t help but chuckle. *This was fun.*
findings.source: 동시에 물음표가 떠오른 세 사람의 얼굴을 마주하자 나도 모르게 실소가 새어 나왔다. 이거 재밌네.

findings.current: As the mage completed the incantation, a wave of qi pulsed through the air.
findings.defect: Using the Murim-specific term “qi” for energy accompanying a modern Hunter spell creates an unsupported system crossover. The source also says the fluctuation accompanies the incantation, not specifically that the incantation was completed.
findings.rationale: “Energy” preserves the source’s generic 기 without misclassifying the spell effect as Murim qi, and the timing remains simultaneous.
findings.replacement: With the mage’s incantation, a ripple of energy passed through the air.
findings.source: 마법사의 영창과 함께 허공에서 느껴지는 기의 파동.

findings.current: “Tell me about it. An F-rank Gate went off near Yangju about an hour ago. I don’t know if something serious is going on.”
findings.defect: The unlisted place name is left as bare romanization despite the packet’s established rendering “Yangju City.”
findings.rationale: “Yangju City” matches the established location rendering and identifies the place naturally without requiring an explanatory footnote.
findings.replacement: “Tell me about it. An F-rank Gate erupted near Yangju City about an hour ago. I don’t know if something serious is going on.”
findings.source: “그러게요. 한 시간 전쯤에 양주 쪽에서 F급 게이트 하나 터졌으니까. 이거 진짜 무슨 일 나는 거 아닌지 모르겠어요.”

findings.current: *Somehow, that name makes me feel like the sun itself is going to regret something.*
findings.defect: The literal wording leaves the joke unintelligible in English. Yoo Sijin’s name prompts an allusion to the drama title “Descendants of the Sun,” with Korean wordplay between 후예 and 후회.
findings.rationale: The replacement makes the cultural allusion and wordplay legible while retaining Taekyung’s dry internal joke.
findings.replacement: *Somehow, his name sounded less like a descendant of the sun and more like the sun’s regret.*
findings.source: 어쩐지 태양이 후회할 것 같은 이름인데.

findings.current: *Is this some kind of mind game?*
findings.defect: “Mind game” suggests psychological manipulation. Here 기만 is Taekyung’s deliberately shabby appearance being perceived as an almost insulting display or humblebrag from someone presumed wealthy.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves the reporter’s comic suspicion that the rich A-rank Hunter is ostentatiously pretending to be ordinary.

findings.defect: The past tense turns Taekyung’s immediate realization into retrospective narration and weakens the final punchline.
findings.rationale: The source is a present-moment realization, and the present tense preserves its abrupt comedic timing.

summary: Several scene facts and speaker assignments are altered, including living ogres being described as already defeated, Captain Yoo’s line being reassigned, the newcomers’ clothing being conflated, and the C-rank/C-cup comparison being reversed. There are also localized register, terminology, and joke-rendering issues.
